chunks: And Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir narrated from Abu al-Sahhari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man bought a house, and a vacant plot remained, so he built a granary on it. Is it considered a waqf (endowment) for the mosque? He said: 'Indeed, the Magians endowed upon the House of Fire.'
ai.seo_question: Does a building constructed on a leftover plot of land count as a mosque endowment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle that the designation of a property as a religious endowment (waqf) is determined by its specific function or nomenclature rather than merely its physical attachment to the main structure. By citing the Magians' designation of their temples as 'houses of fire,' he illustrates that a distinct building on a purchased plot can independently constitute a valid waqf if it is dedicated to a specific religious purpose, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for defining the scope of charitable trusts.
